identity.title: POCUS lung: subpleural consolidation with air bronchograms / hepatization (+/- focal B-lines) for pneumonia

technique.how: Curvilinear or micro-convex 3.5-5 MHz probe; scan anterior, lateral and posterior zones of both hemithoraces in longitudinal view (8-12 zones), patient sitting or supine. Look for a subpleural hypoechoic tissue-like area (hepatization) with hyperechoic air bronchograms, irregular shred sign at the deep border, and focal B-lines; note effusion. Takes up to ~13 min.
technique.prerequisites: Trained operator; posterior access for dependent consolidations.
technique.contraindications: None absolute; open chest wounds or dressings limit windows.

interpretation.positive_finding: Subpleural consolidation with air bronchograms supports pneumonia (pooled LR+ 16.8); a positive scan in a febrile dyspneic patient makes pneumonia likely.
interpretation.negative_finding: A negative scan by a skilled operator substantially lowers pneumonia probability (pooled LR- 0.07, sensitivity 94%), but deep central consolidations not reaching the pleura are missed.
interpretation.pitfalls: Consolidation is not aetiology-specific: atelectasis, infarction from PE, contusion and tumour look similar; static (non-dynamic) air bronchograms suggest atelectasis. Accuracy is lower with briefly trained operators (spec 92%).
interpretation.changes_what: Positive scan supports starting pneumonia treatment without waiting for CXR; negative scan in a skilled operator's hands should redirect toward HF, PE or other causes.

estimates.population: Adults with suspected pneumonia: 6 studies ED/medical wards, 4 studies ICU; mostly expert sonographers
estimates.reference_standard: Chest radiograph and/or chest CT, with or without clinical criteria (CT-only in 3 studies)
estimates.quote: Pooled sensitivity and specificity for the diagnosis of pneumonia using LUS were 94% (95% CI, 92%-96%) and 96% (94%-97%), respectively
estimates.location: Abstract, Results; and Results 'Overall meta-analysis', Figure 2

estimates.reference_standard: Chest CT (3 studies) or imaging plus clinical criteria
estimates.quote: critically-ill patients in the ICU, LUS had a pooled sensitivity of 93% (95% CI, 89% to 95%) and pooled specificity of 97%
estimates.location: Results, 'Subgroup analysis by patient type and physician training'

estimates.target_condition: Pneumonia - ED / medical ward subgroup (6 studies)
estimates.population: Adults presenting to ED or admitted to medical wards with suspected pneumonia
estimates.reference_standard: Chest radiograph and/or chest CT, with or without clinical criteria (CT-only in 3 studies)
estimates.quote: patients admitted to EDs or medical wards, LUS had a pooled sensitivity of 95% (95% CI, 93% to 97%) and pooled specificity of 94%
estimates.location: Results, 'Subgroup analysis by patient type and physician training'

estimates.target_condition: Pneumonia - scans by ED physicians or general practitioners after brief training (2 studies)
estimates.population: Adults with suspected pneumonia scanned by non-expert physicians
estimates.reference_standard: Chest radiograph and/or chest CT, with or without clinical criteria (CT-only in 3 studies)
estimates.quote: ED physicians or general practitioners (n = 2), LUS had a pooled sensitivity of 93% (95% CI, 85% to 97%) and pooled specificity of 92%
estimates.location: Results, 'Subgroup analysis by patient type and physician training'

sources.citation: Chavez MA, Shams N, Ellington LE, Naithani N, Gilman RH, Steinhoff MC, Santosham M, Black RE, et al. Lung ultrasound for the diagnosis of pneumonia in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Respir Res. 2014;15(1):50.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not rely on a negative scan to exclude pneumonia when the operator is inexperienced or posterior zones could not be scanned.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Hypoxaemia, hypotension or altered mentation with consolidation indicates severe pneumonia/sepsis; escalate regardless of scan extent.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Interobserver agreement not pooled in this meta-analysis; only one study described training (3 h didactic + 3 h hands-on).
safety_scope.skill_assumption: Pooled estimates reflect expert sonographers in 7/10 studies; two studies with briefly trained ED physicians/GPs showed lower specificity (92%). Assume a trained operator using an 8-12 zone protocol.

extraction_notes: Full text read via PMC (PMC4005846). LR quote for the overall estimate: 'pooled positive and negative LRs were 16.8 (7.7-37.0) and 0.07 (0.05-0.10), respectively' (Abstract, Results; Figure 2). Subgroup LRs were not reported, only sens/spec. Prevalence not pooled in the paper, left null. Further subgroups reported: CT-only reference standard sens 94% (90-97) spec 99% (97-100); consolidation-only studies sens 94% (92-96) spec 98% (97-99) (Results, 'Subgroup analysis by diagnostic imaging criteria'). Threshold/protocol: pneumonia defined on LUS as consolidation (with air bronchograms) +/- focal B-lines per Table 3 'Diagnostic criteria' column; LUS took a maximum of 13 minutes (Abstract).
